rows.uncertainty: Abstract only; full text paywalled (Europe PMC: subscription required; LWW HTTP 403). Very small sample: a 'pilot study' in which '6 patients were treated'. Significance is claimed for lesions ('an ANOVA model') while lesions come from only 6 patients; the abstract does not say how many lesions each patient contributed [several per patient, inferred from 6 patients and a lesion-level analysis] or whether the analysis accounted for clustering of lesions within patients. One comparison is against 'baseline' (before-after), not only against untreated lesions; the untreated-lesion comparison is the controlled one. No effect size, p-value, lesion count or repigmentation percentage reported in abstract; 'significantly higher' is stated without numbers. The Conclusion's 'acceptable cosmetic outcomes' and 'effective treatment option' are not backed by any result reported in the abstract; participant self-grades are mentioned but not reported. Abstract does not say whether 'end of the study' is the final treatment visit or later, so months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE; no durability data. Funding and conflicts of interest: not in abstract (first author affiliated with a private practice, Westlake Dermatology). Abstract does not name a trial registration; registry record NCT01956435 is a separate unit and was not used.
rows.citation: Gordon JR, Reed KE, Sebastian KR, Ahmed AM. Dermatol Surg 2017;43(4):553-557

quotes.quote: 6 patients were treated with excimer laser for 12 weeks using the vitiligo protocol
Lesions that received the excimer treatment had significantly higher repigmentation by the end of the study compared with baseline and untreated lesions.
Effectiveness was graded by the blinded observer scale through photographic comparisons at the end of the study.
